chapter.tudor.title: The Tudors
level.actium.fact: On September 2, 31 BC, off Cape Actium, Octavian's fleet, led by Agrippa, decisively defeated the ships of Antony and Cleopatra. In the midst of the battle, Cleopatra withdrew her squadron, Antony rushed after her — and both fled to Egypt, having lost the war.
level.actium.goal: Antony's fleet utterly defeated at Actium
level.actium.hint: Antony tied his fate to the East — and on the sea, it will be his undoing.
level.actium.title: Actium
level.alexandria.fact: In August 30 BC, Antony, believing a false report of Cleopatra's death, fell upon his sword. The Queen, unwilling to be paraded through Rome in a triumphal procession, took her own life — according to legend, by allowing an asp to bite her. With her death, Ptolemaic Egypt fell, and Octavian became Augustus, the first Emperor of Rome.
level.alexandria.goal: Antony and Cleopatra meet their end in Alexandria
level.alexandria.hint: First, bid farewell: bring the queen to the fallen general. Then she will follow him.
level.alexandria.intro: All is lost; Octavian is at the gates of Alexandria.
level.alexandria.title: Cleopatra's Asp
level.alexei.fact: In 1718, Tsarevich Alexei, who had fled abroad and was accused of treason against his reformist father, was returned, condemned to death, and died in the Peter and Paul Fortress under unclear circumstances.
level.alexei.goal: The reformist Tsar judges his own son
level.alexei.hint: No revolt here – the court decides the heir's fate.
level.alexei.title: The Case of Tsarevich Alexei
level.anne_boleyn.fact: Anne Boleyn, for whom Henry broke with Rome, bore a daughter, Elizabeth, but no son. Losing interest in her, the king allowed Thomas Cromwell to fabricate charges of treason, incest, and witchcraft. On May 19, 1536, Anne was beheaded in the Tower. The accusations were almost certainly false.
level.anne_boleyn.goal: For her, Rome fell — and on the block, she too.
level.anne_boleyn.hint: The minister, not the king, brings the accusation. Then — the Tower.
level.anne_boleyn.source: E. Ives, 'The Life and Death of Anne Boleyn'
level.anne_boleyn.title: Anne Boleyn
level.anne_cleves.fact: The marriage to Anne of Cleves (1540) was arranged by Cromwell based on a flattering portrait by Holbein. In person, Anne did not please the king (the myth of the 'Flanders mare' was malicious gossip); the marriage was annulled after six months as unconsummated. Anne agreed and became the 'King's good sister,' outliving all of Henry's wives. Cromwell, however, paid with his head for this marriage.
level.anne_cleves.goal: An unwanted marriage quietly annulled — Anne remains whole.
level.anne_cleves.hint: First, the minister will present her at court, then the wedding, then — the annulment. The executioner's block is not for her.
level.anne_cleves.intro: Cromwell proposes a bride from overseas to the king, one he has not seen.
level.anne_cleves.source: A. Weir, 'The Six Wives of Henry VIII'
level.anne_cleves.title: Anne of Cleves
level.antoinette.fact: On October 16, 1793, Marie Antoinette, the 'Widow Capet,' was guillotined nine months after her husband. The Revolutionary Tribunal accused her of treason and conspiracy with foreign powers.
level.antoinette.goal: The former queen is tried and executed
level.antoinette.hint: The Jacobin Club has no part in this — lead her through trial and to the scaffold.
level.antoinette.title: The Widow Capet
level.aragon_divorce.fact: Pope Clement VII refused to annul Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon. In 1533–34, Henry broke with Rome: by the 'Act of Supremacy,' he declared himself Supreme Head of the Church of England, personally declared the marriage invalid, and married Anne Boleyn. Thus began the English Reformation.
level.aragon_divorce.goal: Henry breaks with Rome and divorces Catherine.
level.aragon_divorce.hint: The Pope will not grant a divorce. Become head of the Church yourself — and only then judge your marriage.
level.aragon_divorce.intro: Henry is married to Catherine, but yearns for a divorce — and the Pope is against it.
level.aragon_divorce.title: The Divorce from Rome
level.armada.fact: In 1588, Philip II of Spain launched the "Invincible Armada" of 130 ships against England. The English fleet, where Francis Drake distinguished himself, scattered the Spanish with fireships off Gravelines, and a storm completed their rout. The victory saved Protestant England and elevated Elizabeth to the pinnacle of glory.
level.armada.goal: Drake's fireships scatter the Armada — Elizabeth triumphs
level.armada.hint: First, Drake will launch fireships and scatter Philip's fleet; then, English ships will finish off the Armada.
level.armada.intro: Philip II sends the "Invincible Armada" to punish the heretic Elizabeth. Francis Drake awaits off the coast.
level.armada.title: The Invincible Armada
level.bloody_mary.fact: Mary I (1553–1558) returned England to the authority of Rome and married Philip II of Spain. Her reign was dubbed "Bloody": about 280 Protestants were burned at the stake, including Archbishop Thomas Cranmer (1556), author of the English prayer book. She never bore an heir.
level.bloody_mary.goal: Mary is crowned, marries Philip, returns England to Rome — and burns Cranmer
level.bloody_mary.hint: Be crowned, marry Philip, and send the Protestant archbishop to the stake — this will return England to Rome.
level.bloody_mary.intro: Mary I is Queen. She will return England to Rome, marry Philip of Spain — and deal with the heretics.
level.bloody_mary.title: Bloody Mary
level.bonfire.fact: On May 23, 1498, Girolamo Savonarola was hanged and burned in the Piazza della Signoria in Florence, his ashes cast into the Arno River to prevent any relics from remaining. Thus, the Pope dealt with his accuser.
level.bonfire.goal: The excommunicated preacher faces the pyre
level.bonfire.hint: First, excommunication; then, the pyre in the piazza.
level.bonfire.intro: The pyre awaits the excommunicated Savonarola.
level.bonfire.title: Savonarola's Pyre
level.bosworth.fact: On 22 August 1485 the Battle of Bosworth was decided by betrayal: Lord Thomas Stanley held back to the last moment, then threw his forces onto Henry Tudor's side. Richard III fell in battle — the last English king to die on the field. His crown, by tradition, was found in a hawthorn bush and placed on Henry right there on the field. So ended the Wars of the Roses and began the Tudor dynasty.
level.bosworth.goal: Stanley's betrayal decides Bosworth — the crown passes to Henry Tudor
level.bosworth.hint: First let Stanley defect to Henry — otherwise Richard wins. Then the battle, and only then is the fallen king's crown placed on the victor.
level.bosworth.intro: Richard III reigns. Henry Tudor marches for the crown — but all will hinge on whose side Lord Stanley takes.
level.bosworth.title: Bosworth
level.brumaire.fact: On November 9–10, 1799 (18–19 Brumaire, Year VIII), Napoleon staged a coup, dissolving the Directory and establishing the Consulate. He appointed himself First Consul — the de facto dictator of France.
level.brumaire.goal: The General seizes power and becomes First Consul
level.brumaire.hint: First — glory at Toulon, then — a coup d'état.
level.brumaire.title: 18 Brumaire
level.caesar_assassination.fact: On March 15, 44 BC (the Ides of March), Julius Caesar was assassinated in the Senate by a group of conspirators — over 60 senators led by Brutus and Cassius. The phrase 'Et tu, Brute?' is Shakespeare's literary version; Suetonius reports the words 'And you, child?' in Greek.
level.caesar_assassination.goal: Friend Brutus joins the conspiracy and kills Caesar.
level.caesar_assassination.hint: Brutus weaves the conspiracy with Cassius — not with Caesar himself. Antony must not be part of the conspiracy.
level.caesar_assassination.source: Suetonius, 'The Lives of the Twelve Caesars'
level.caesar_assassination.title: Et tu, Brute?
level.caesar_crown.fact: At Lupercalia in February 44 BC, Mark Antony thrice offered Caesar a royal diadem — and Caesar thrice publicly refused it to the approving roar of the crowd. He never became King of Rome, but persistent rumors of royal ambitions (not least due to Cleopatra's presence in Rome) spurred the conspirators to action.
level.caesar_crown.goal: The people love Caesar — but he will not be king
level.caesar_crown.hint: First, the queen's chambers, in private: Caesar is captivated and ambitious. Then Antony will rally the people around him in the Forum. Only then, at Lupercalia, will loyal Antony present the crown — Caesar will gracefully refuse. Keep Cleopatra from the crown.
level.caesar_crown.title: King of Rome?
level.cicero_death.fact: In 43 BC, Cicero assailed Mark Antony with fourteen "Philippics." Upon forming the Triumvirate, Antony demanded his head — and Octavian, whom Cicero had supported, surrendered the old orator. On December 7, assassins caught Cicero near Formiae; by Antony's order, his head and the hands that wrote his speeches were nailed to the Rostra in the Forum, and Fulvia, according to legend, pierced his tongue with a hairpin.
level.cicero_death.goal: Cicero's words against Antony cost him his head
level.cicero_death.hint: Let Cicero denounce Antony from the Rostra; an enraged Antony, with Octavian, will place him on the proscription lists — and only then will assassins catch the orator.
level.cicero_death.intro: Cicero assails Antony from the tribune — but the Triumvirs are already dividing their enemies on the proscription lists.
level.cicero_death.title: The Price of Words
level.cleopatra_charm.fact: In 48 BC, Cleopatra could not openly enter Caesar's presence — the palace of Alexandria was held by her rival brother Ptolemy XIII. Her loyal servant Apollodorus secretly carried the queen past the guards, wrapped in a bedding sack (according to Plutarch, in a carpet). Only once inside did she charm Caesar; their son Caesarion was born in 47 BC.
level.cleopatra_charm.goal: Cleopatra secretly gains access to Caesar
level.cleopatra_charm.hint: First, she must be secretly brought inside — and no one extra is needed in the bedchamber
level.cleopatra_charm.intro: Cleopatra is a foreigner; the palace guards will not let her in
level.cleopatra_charm.title: The Queen and the Dictator
level.cleopatra_rome.fact: In 46 BC, Cleopatra arrived in Rome with her son Caesarion and lived in Caesar's villa beyond the Tiber; Caesar erected a golden statue of her in the Temple of Venus. The honors bestowed upon a foreign queen and the dictatorial, kingly pretensions angered the senators and fueled the conspiracy.
level.cleopatra_rome.goal: Royal honors for Cleopatra push the Senate toward a plot
level.cleopatra_rome.hint: First bring the queen to Rome, then raise her to honors. Only upon seeing Caesar in royal splendor will the senators reach for their daggers.
level.cleopatra_rome.title: Cleopatra in Rome
level.cleopatra_throne.fact: During the Alexandrian War (48–47 BC), Caesar defeated the forces of Ptolemy XIII; the fleeing king drowned in the Nile. Caesar established Cleopatra on the Egyptian throne.
level.cleopatra_throne.hint: First, eliminate the rival, then secure Rome's support
level.cleopatra_throne.source: Caesar, 'Commentaries on the Civil War'; Cassius Dio
level.cleopatra_throne.title: War for the Throne
level.conclave.fact: In 1492, Rodrigo Borgia secured his election as Pope Alexander VI through lavish bribes to the cardinals. His pontificate became a symbol of the venality and corruption of the Renaissance Church.
level.conclave.goal: Rodrigo Borgia buys the papal throne
level.conclave.hint: Let Rodrigo first buy the cardinals' votes — and only a paid conclave will raise him to the throne. della Rovere cannot outbid the Borgia's coffers.
level.conclave.intro: 1492. The Throne of Peter is vacant. Cardinal Rodrigo Borgia and his old enemy della Rovere vie for the tiara. Rodrigo has gold.
level.conclave.title: Alexander VI
level.coronation.fact: On January 16, 1547, Grand Prince Ivan IV was crowned Tsar in the Dormition Cathedral of the Kremlin, being the first to adopt the title "Tsar of All Rus'." Thus, the Tsardom of Russia was born.
level.coronation.goal: The Sovereign of All Rus' receives the Tsar's crown
level.coronation.hint: Let Ivan besiege boyar Shuisky in the Duma and become an autocrat — only then will he be crowned tsar. The boyar will not wear the crown.
level.coronation.intro: Young Ivan grew up under wayward boyar-regents. To become tsar, he must first break their power.
level.coronation.source: The Rite of Coronation of Ivan IV, 1547
level.coronation.title: Coronation as Tsar
level.coup.fact: On June 28, 1762, the Guards enthroned Catherine, deposing her husband Peter III. A week later, the former emperor died in Ropsha. Thus began 34 years of the 'Golden Age' of the nobility.
level.coup.goal: The Guards depose Peter III — Catherine takes the throne
level.coup.hint: Let Orlov first raise the guard for Catherine — and only supported by bayonets will she depose and ruin Peter III. Without the guard, the coup will fail.
level.coup.intro: Peter III is unpopular and weak. His wife Catherine and guardsman Orlov are preparing a coup.
level.coup.title: The Coup of 1762
level.danton.fact: On April 5, 1794, Georges Danton, one of the Revolution's leaders who advocated for tempering the Terror, was executed at Robespierre's behest. 'You will show my head to the people: it is worth it,' he declared to the executioner.
level.danton.goal: Robespierre sends his former comrade to the guillotine
level.danton.hint: Radicalize in the Club, accuse Danton in the Convention, then — the scaffold.
level.danton.title: Danton on the Scaffold
level.discord.fact: By 33–32 BC, the alliance of the triumvirs collapsed. Octavian launched propaganda against Antony: he published his will, portraying him as a slave to a foreign queen who had forgotten Rome. The Senate declared war — formally against Cleopatra.
level.discord.goal: Octavian does not forgive Antony his Eastern queen
level.discord.hint: First, Antony leaves for Cleopatra — then Rome turns away from him.
level.discord.title: The Rift
level.disgrace.fact: Fearing Belisarius's excessive fame and popularity, Justinian repeatedly recalled him, stripped him of his troops, and held him in disfavor. Legend even depicted the great general as a blind beggar — a symbol of the ingratitude of power.
level.disgrace.goal: The jealous emperor sidelines a too-glorious hero
level.disgrace.hint: Let Narses first slander the hero with an accusation — and only then will a suspicious Justinian strip the disgraced Belisarius of his honors. Mundus is not so renowned as to be feared.
level.disgrace.intro: Belisarius's glory eclipses the throne. His rival, Narses, is ready to whisper the right words to the emperor.
level.disgrace.title: The Disgrace of Belisarius
level.downfall.fact: Deprived of his father, the Pope, Cesare Borgia was arrested by Julius II, lost all his possessions, and fled to Spain, where he died in a minor skirmish in 1507. Thus, the dominion admired by Machiavelli collapsed overnight.
level.downfall.goal: Cesare, having lost his patron, is overthrown
level.downfall.hint: Let Julius first seize the duke who has lost his father — and only the captive will be stripped of all lands and power. The uncaptured cannot be deposed.
level.downfall.intro: The Warrior Pope Julius II hates the Borgia. With his father's death, Cesare lost his protector — and the hour of reckoning has come.
level.downfall.title: Cesare's Downfall
level.elizabeth.fact: Elizabeth I (1558–1603) was crowned and, through the "Elizabethan Religious Settlement," reconciled Protestants and Catholics. She rejected suitors — including Philip II and her favorite Robert Dudley — throughout her life, remaining the "Virgin Queen": an unmarried monarch is her own mistress.
level.elizabeth.goal: Elizabeth is crowned, reconciles the Church — and remains unmarried
level.elizabeth.hint: Crown her and settle the Church. Keep Dudley as a favorite at court — but lead neither him nor Philip to the altar.
level.elizabeth.intro: Elizabeth I is crowned Queen. Suitors besiege her: both Philip of Spain and her beloved Robert Dudley — but the crown is dearer.
level.elizabeth.title: The Virgin Queen
level.emperor.fact: On October 22, 1721, after the victory in the Great Northern War, the Senate bestowed upon Peter I the title 'Emperor of All Russia, Father of the Fatherland, the Great'. The Russian Tsardom became the Russian Empire.
level.emperor.goal: The Senate proclaims the victor over the Swedes as Emperor
level.emperor.hint: First, victory over Charles; then, the imperial title in the Senate.
level.emperor.title: Emperor of All Russia
level.empress.fact: At the same ceremony on December 2, 1804, Napoleon crowned his wife, Joséphine de Beauharnais, Empress, placing the crown upon her head himself. Their marriage, however, was annulled in 1809 due to the lack of an heir.
level.empress.hint: Let Napoleon first seize the crown and crown himself — and only then shall the crowned emperor place the diadem on Josephine. The order cannot be broken.
level.empress.intro: Notre Dame, 1804. The Pope is ready to bestow the crown — but Napoleon has conceived an unprecedented audacity.
level.empress.title: Empress Joséphine
level.excommunicate.fact: The Florentine monk Girolamo Savonarola fiercely denounced the corruption of the Borgias and the entire Church, organizing 'bonfires of the vanities.' In 1497, Alexander VI excommunicated him.
level.excommunicate.goal: The Pope excommunicates the audacious preacher
level.excommunicate.hint: Let Savonarola first boldly denounce the Pope from the pulpit — and only the rebel will the Pope anathematize. Until the monk issues a challenge, there is no anathema.
level.excommunicate.intro: The monk Savonarola burns 'bonfires of the vanities' and from the pulpit denounces the corrupt Pope. Rome is divided.
level.excommunicate.title: Excommunication
level.execution.fact: On January 10, 1775, Yemelyan Pugachev was executed in Bolotnaya Square in Moscow. The rebellion was drowned in blood; Catherine II renamed the Yaik River to the Ural to erase the memory of the revolt.
level.execution.goal: The captured impostor is executed in Bolotnaya Square
level.execution.hint: First — capture by Suvorov, then — the block by the sovereign's will.
level.execution.intro: The Empress reigns; the captured impostor awaits judgment.
level.execution.title: The Execution of Pugachev
level.flight.fact: When Justinian was preparing to flee, Theodora stopped the council with the words: «Imperial purple makes the best shroud», preferring death on the throne to flight. Her resolve saved the throne.
level.flight.goal: Theodora restrains the emperor ready to flee
level.flight.hint: Who will stay the wavering emperor? Not the advisors who urge flight — only Theodora with the words, 'Purple makes the noblest shroud.'
level.flight.intro: The rebellion rages, the ship stands ready. The council — Narses the eunuch, Belisarius the general — whispers to flee. Only one voice commands them to stay.
level.flight.title: Purple Makes the Best Shroud
level.fratricide.fact: In June 1497, Juan Borgia was murdered, his body cast into the Tiber. Rumor accused his brother Cesare, who eliminated a rival for their father's affection and power. The murder remained unsolved.
level.fratricide.goal: Cesare secretly murders his rival brother
level.fratricide.hint: Let the fraternal feast ignite Cesare's envy — and only consumed by it will he dispose of Juan in the Tiber. Without resentment, his hand will not rise.
level.fratricide.intro: His father made Juan Gonfalonier of the Church, bypassing the capable Cesare. The younger brother's envy grows.
level.fratricide.title: Body in the Tiber
level.giulia.fact: Giulia Farnese, the young mistress of Alexander VI, was sardonically dubbed 'Bride of Christ' by the Romans. Through her, her brother achieved a meteoric career and himself became Pope Paul III.
level.giulia.goal: A young beauty becomes the Pope's favorite
level.giulia.hint: Let Giulia first captivate the Pope during a rendezvous — and only enamored will he shower her with favors. Lucrezia is his daughter, not a mistress.
level.giulia.intro: Young Giulia Farnese captivated the old Pope. The key to papal favors lies through the pontiff's heart.
level.giulia.title: Bride of Christ
level.hagia.fact: After the Nika fire, Justinian rebuilt the Hagia Sophia (537) — for a thousand years the greatest temple of Christianity. Upon entering its colossal dome, the emperor, according to legend, exclaimed: «Solomon, I have surpassed you!».
level.hagia.goal: The emperor erects the greatest temple of Christianity
level.hagia.hint: Let the emperor himself conceive the cathedral amidst the ruins — and only then will he erect the Hagia Sophia. Courtiers do not build temples.
level.hagia.intro: The Nika riot burned the old temple to ashes. Amidst the ruins, Justinian conceives the unprecedented.
level.hagia.title: Hagia Sophia
level.heir.fact: Justin I, an illiterate soldier who became emperor, brought close and adopted his gifted nephew Justinian, making him co-ruler and heir to the throne.
level.heir.goal: Old Justin makes his nephew heir
level.heir.hint: First, let Justin entrust the gifted Justinian with the palace guard — and only then declare the proven man his heir. Germanus is superfluous here.
level.heir.intro: The illiterate soldier Justin became emperor — but which of his nephews should he make his heir? Ambitious Germanus also awaits his hour.
level.heir.source: History of the Eastern Roman Empire
level.heir.title: Justin's Heir
level.howard.fact: Catherine Howard, the fifth wife, was very young. Her pre-marital affairs and accusations of treason with courtier Thomas Culpeper surfaced. On February 13, 1542, she was beheaded in the Tower. According to legend, the day before, she requested the block be brought so she could 'dignifiedly' rehearse her execution.
level.howard.goal: The young queen — and the block once more
level.howard.hint: The accusation — from the minister, the execution — in the Tower. They will grant her no reprieve.
level.howard.title: Catherine Howard
level.hypatius.fact: On January 10, 1775, Yemelyan Pugachev was executed on Bolotnaya Square in Moscow. The rebellion was drowned in blood; Catherine II renamed the Yaik River to the Ural to erase the memory of the revolt.
level.hypatius.goal: The captured impostor is executed on Bolotnaya Square
level.hypatius.hint: First, let Theodora reject mercy and harden the emperor's resolve — and only then will Justinian send the usurper to the block. Without her word, he would pardon him.
level.hypatius.intro: Hypatius is captured. He swears the mob raised him by force — and Justinian is ready to forgive. But Theodora holds a different view.
level.hypatius.title: Pugachev's Execution
level.jacobins.fact: The Jacobin Club became the engine of the Revolution. Robespierre and his young comrade Louis de Saint-Just transformed it into a stronghold of radicals, from which the Terror emanated. Saint-Just was dubbed the 'Archangel of Terror.'
level.jacobins.hint: Let Robespierre first ignite into a radical in the debate — and only then shall he infect Saint-Just with radicalism. The Girondin Corday cannot be turned into a Jacobin.
level.jacobins.intro: The Jacobin Club is seething. Robespierre inflames his comrades, while moderate Girondins try to cool him down.
level.jacobins.title: The Jacobin Club
level.jane_grey.fact: In July 1553, the Duke of Northumberland proclaimed Lady Jane Grey — his daughter-in-law — as Queen. But the people and nobility rallied behind Henry VIII's daughter, Mary; nine days later, Jane was deposed. Northumberland was executed immediately; sixteen-year-old Jane, in February 1554. Mary I ascended the throne.
level.jane_grey.goal: Northumberland's puppet is overthrown by Mary — and Jane ascends the scaffold
level.jane_grey.hint: Let Northumberland proclaim Jane Queen; then Mary will depose her and send her to the block.
level.jane_grey.intro: Edward VI is dead. The Duke of Northumberland places his daughter-in-law, Jane Grey, on the throne — bypassing the rightful Mary.
level.jane_grey.title: The Nine Days' Queen
level.jane_seymour.fact: On May 19, 1536, Anne Boleyn was beheaded at the Tower; just 11 days later, Henry VIII married Jane Seymour. In October 1537, she gave birth to the long-awaited son — the future Edward VI — and died twelve days later of puerperal fever. Jane was the only wife Henry mourned.
level.jane_seymour.goal: After executing Boleyn, Henry marries Jane — she bears an heir and dies.
level.jane_seymour.hint: First, execute the condemned Boleyn, then marry Jane, and only then — the heir (her childbirth will be her undoing).
level.jane_seymour.intro: Anne Boleyn is condemned. Henry already gazes upon Jane Seymour — but the path to a new wedding lies through the executioner's block.
level.jane_seymour.title: Jane Seymour
level.john_fall.fact: Theodora and her friend Antonina, Belisarius's wife, used intrigue to lure John of Cappadocia into a fabricated conspiracy against the emperor. Exposed, the all-powerful minister fell and was sent into exile.
level.john_fall.goal: Theodora and Antonina ruin the hated minister
level.john_fall.hint: Let Antonina first lull John's vigilance with false friendship — and only then lure him into a nocturnal trap. Tribonian is not her target.
level.john_fall.intro: Theodora yearns for the downfall of John the Cappadocian. Her confidante Antonina, Belisarius's wife, weaves a snare — with feigned friendship.
level.john_fall.title: Trap for John
level.juan.fact: Alexander VI openly preferred his younger son Juan, making him Gonfalonier of the Church and a Duke. This ignited a burning envy in his elder brother, Cesare.
level.juan.goal: The Pope showers Cesare's brother, Juan, with favors
level.juan.hint: The favor goes not to the cardinal, but to his brother.
level.juan.intro: Alexander VI is on the throne and showers his favorite son with favors.
level.juan.source: History of the House of Borgia
level.juan.title: The Favorite Son
level.julius.fact: In 1503, Giuliano della Rovere became Pope Julius II, a long-standing enemy of the Borgias. The 'Warrior Pope' and patron of Michelangelo, he aimed to destroy everything Cesare had created.
level.julius.goal: The sworn enemy of the Borgias ascends to the throne
level.julius.hint: Let della Rovere first unite the enemies of the Borgia — and only having risen will he take the throne as Julius II. Cesare is a Borgia; he will not see the tiara.
level.julius.intro: Alexander VI is dead. The sworn enemy of the Borgia, della Rovere, sees his hour — but Cesare is still strong in the conclave.
level.julius.source: History of the Pontificate of Julius II
level.julius.title: Julius II
level.kazan.fact: On October 2, 1552, Ivan the Terrible's troops captured Kazan, annexing the Kazan Khanate to the Russian Tsardom. This opened the way to the east and to the conquest of Astrakhan and Siberia.
level.kazan.goal: The Tsar conquers the Kazan Khanate
level.kazan.hint: First, the tsar must be crowned in the cathedral — and only the reigning Ivan will conquer Kazan. Boyar Shuisky will not lead the troops.
level.kazan.intro: The crowned tsar needs a great victory. The Kazan Khanate is a long-standing enemy at the eastern borders.
level.kazan.source: Chronicles of the Taking of Kazan
level.kazan.title: The Taking of Kazan
level.king_trial.fact: On January 21, 1793, Louis XVI, condemned by the National Convention as 'Citizen Louis Capet,' was guillotined in the Place de la Révolution. The king's execution shocked the monarchies of Europe and accelerated the war.
level.king_trial.goal: The Convention tries the king and sends him to the guillotine
level.king_trial.hint: First — a verdict in the Convention, then — the scaffold.
level.king_trial.title: Execution of Louis XVI
level.lucrezia.fact: Lucrezia Borgia was married off three times by her father and brother for political alliances; one husband, deemed superfluous, was strangled. Rumor attributed poisons and debauchery to her—likely slander from the family's enemies.
level.lucrezia.goal: The Pope marries off his daughter for political gain
level.lucrezia.hint: Let the Pope first negotiate a marriage alliance — and only the betrothed Lucrezia will be led to the altar. Giulia, the mistress, is not given in marriage.
level.lucrezia.intro: The Pope trades his daughter's hand like a bargaining chip. Lucrezia is a pawn in the great game of alliances.
level.lucrezia.title: Child of Politics
level.marat.fact: On July 13, 1793, the Girondist Charlotte Corday stabbed Jean-Paul Marat in his bath, where he was immersed due to a skin condition. Four days later, Corday was guillotined. Marat's death was immortalized by Jacques-Louis David.
level.marat.goal: Charlotte Corday kills Marat — and ascends the scaffold
level.marat.hint: Corday finds Marat in his bath; for this, the guillotine awaits her.
level.marat.title: The Death of Marat
level.marriage.fact: Theodora, daughter of a bear-keeper and a former actress, captivated Justinian. For the sake of marrying her, he secured the repeal of a law that forbade senators from marrying actresses. She became one of the most influential women in history.
level.marriage.goal: Justinian marries the former actress Theodora
level.marriage.hint: First, change the law, elevating Theodora to patrician status — and only then lead her to the altar. Do not mistake the bride.
level.marriage.intro: Justinian fell in love with Theodora — an actress, daughter of a bear-keeper. But ancient law forbade nobles from marrying actresses.
level.marriage.title: Actress on the Throne
level.mary_stuart.fact: Mary, Queen of Scots, the deposed Queen of Scotland, was Elizabeth's prisoner for 19 years and the focal point of Catholic conspiracies. Francis Walsingham's spy network intercepted her encrypted letters, which approved the Babington Plot against Elizabeth. The court sentenced Mary to death; she was beheaded in 1587.
level.mary_stuart.goal: Walsingham exposes Mary, Queen of Scots — trial and scaffold.
level.mary_stuart.hint: First, Walsingham will intercept the letters and expose Mary, and only then — the scaffold.
level.mary_stuart.intro: Mary, Queen of Scots, prisoner and claimant, weaves a plot against Elizabeth. The spy Walsingham reads her letters.
level.mary_stuart.title: Mary Stuart
level.massacre.fact: Belisarius and Mundus trapped the rebels in the Hippodrome and orchestrated a massacre—according to accounts, up to 30,000 people perished. The Nika Revolt was drowned in blood, and Justinian's throne was saved.
level.massacre.goal: Belisarius Drowns the Revolt in Blood
level.massacre.hint: Let Narses bribe the Blues with gold — and only then will Belisarius (or Mundus) trap and crush the divided mob. Without bribery, the rebellion cannot be broken.
level.massacre.intro: The mob proclaimed Hypatius and filled the Hippodrome. To assault them head-on is suicide. First, they must be divided.
level.massacre.title: Massacre at the Hippodrome
level.minister.fact: John the Cappadocian, Justinian's all-powerful finance minister, extorted exorbitant taxes from the people. His greed and cruelty made him the most hated man in Constantinople—and one of the causes of the revolt.
level.minister.goal: The All-Powerful Minister Strangles the City with Levies
level.minister.hint: Let John himself fleece the people with treasury levies — and then the mob will hate him. Tribonian is known for other things.
level.minister.intro: Justinian's court is held by two hated officials: the corrupt John the Cappadocian and the jurist Tribonian. The people murmur against the levies.
level.minister.title: The Hated Minister
level.nepotism.fact: At 18, Cesare Borgia became a cardinal by his father-Pope's will—a blatant example of nepotism. He hated his ecclesiastical career, dreaming of a sword, not a cassock.
level.nepotism.goal: The Pope elevates his young son to cardinal
level.nepotism.hint: First the throne, then the Pope bestows the cardinal's hat upon his son.
level.nepotism.title: Cardinal at Eighteen
level.nika.fact: In January 532 AD, the circus factions of the 'Blues' and 'Greens,' usually hostile, united with the cry 'Nika!' ('Conquer!'). Half the city burned; the mob, against its will, proclaimed the noble Hypatius, nephew of the former emperor, as their ruler.
level.nika.goal: The Rebellious Mob Proclaims Hypatius Emperor
level.nika.hint: Let the fury against the corrupt John ignite the rebellion — and then the already incensed mob will proclaim Hypatius. Germanus is noble, but the crowd did not raise him.
level.nika.intro: January 532 AD. The Blues and Greens, eternal rivals, united against the levies of the hated John. The mob demands an emperor in place of Justinian.
level.nika.title: The Nika Revolt
level.oath.fact: On June 20, 1789, deputies of the Third Estate, locked out of their assembly hall, gathered in the Royal Tennis Court and swore not to disperse until they had given France a constitution. The 'Tennis Court Oath' became the first act of the Revolution.
level.oath.goal: Deputies unite into a revolutionary bloc
level.oath.hint: Let the royal lockout in the hall embitter the deputy — and only then shall the unyielding swear in the tennis court not to disperse. The King will not take the oath.
level.oath.intro: June 1789. The King locks the assembly hall before the deputies of the Third Estate. But they cannot be broken so easily.
level.oath.title: Oath of the Third Estate
level.oprichnina.fact: In 1565, Ivan the Terrible established the Oprichnina – a special domain with a personal army. The Oprichniki, led by Malyuta Skuratov, sowed terror; the Novgorod massacre of 1570 claimed thousands of lives.
level.oprichnina.goal: The Tsar introduces the Oprichnina and unleashes terror.
level.oprichnina.hint: Let boyar treason in the Duma embitter the tsar — and only the loyal Ivan with Malyuta will establish the oprichnina. Shuisky is not fit to be an oprichnik.
level.oprichnina.intro: The boyars are plotting sedition, and Ivan sees treason everywhere. He needs an instrument of reprisal — and his loyal hound Malyuta.
level.oprichnina.title: The Oprichnina
level.parr.fact: Catherine Parr, the sixth wife, sympathized with Protestants; conservative enemies at court obtained a warrant for her arrest on charges of heresy. Upon learning of this, she humbly confessed to the King, stating that she had only argued to distract him from his pains. Henry forgave her. She outlived the King (d. 1547) — she 'survived'.
level.parr.goal: Enemies weave a net — but the Queen will survive
level.parr.hint: She too will be accused. But the block is a trap: salvation lies in reconciliation with the King at court.
level.parr.title: Catherine Parr
level.pharsalus.fact: On August 9, 48 BC, at Pharsalus in Thessaly, Caesar's smaller but veteran army routed Pompey's force twice its size. Caesar's left wing was commanded by Mark Antony. Pompey fled the field and sailed east — to Egypt.
level.pharsalus.hint: First form the line with a loyal wing commander — only then will the legions crush Pompey on the field.
level.pharsalus.source: Caesar, 'Commentaries on the Civil War'; Appian
level.pharsalus.title: Pharsalus
level.philippi.fact: In the autumn of 42 BC, at Philippi, the armies of Antony and Octavian defeated the conspirators' army. Cassius committed suicide after the first battle, Brutus after the second. According to Plutarch, Antony covered Brutus' body with his purple cloak as a sign of respect.
level.philippi.goal: The traitor Brutus is defeated — Caesar is avenged
level.philippi.hint: Neither Caesar nor Antony are part of the conspiracy
level.philippi.title: Revenge for Caesar
level.poison.fact: The Borgias eliminated wealthy cardinals with the famous poison 'cantarella' to seize their assets. Cardinal Orsini became one of the victims of this practice of 'inheritance through poisoning'.
level.poison.goal: The Borgias poison a rival at a feast
level.poison.hint: Let Cesare first invite the cardinal to a friendly feast and lull his vigilance — and only to the trusting will he offer the cantarella. The poison will not work on the wary.
level.poison.intro: Cardinal Orsini is rich, and the Borgia need money. Cesare's hospitality is deadly.
level.poison.title: Cantarella
level.poison_death.fact: In August 1503, Alexander VI suddenly died of a fever. According to a persistent legend, the Pope and Cesare Borgia mistakenly drank wine they had poisoned for a wealthy cardinal. Cesare survived but lost everything. Historians, however, attribute his death to malaria.
level.poison_death.goal: The Pope drinks wine poisoned for another
level.poison_death.hint: Let Cesare first prepare poison for the cardinal — and by a fatal error, the poisoned wine at the feast will be drunk by the Pope himself. Without the son's plot, the feast is harmless.
level.poison_death.intro: The Borgia planned to eliminate a rich cardinal at a feast with poisoned wine. But fate had other plans.
level.poison_death.title: The Fatal Feast
level.poltava.fact: On June 27, 1709, Peter I's army decisively defeated Charles XII's Swedes near Poltava. This victory turned the tide of the Great Northern War and transformed Russia into a great European power.
level.poltava.goal: Peter utterly defeats the Swedish king.
level.poltava.hint: Let Peter first assemble and train a regular army — and only a ready army will defeat the Swede Charles at Poltava. The traitor Mazepa is not the target.
level.poltava.intro: Charles XII invaded Russia, and Hetman Mazepa betrayed Peter and led the Cossacks to the Swede. The fate of the war is being decided.
level.poltava.source: Report on the Battle of Poltava
level.poltava.title: Poltava
level.pompey_death.fact: On September 28, 48 BC, Pompey landed in Egypt, hoping for asylum. By order of the courtiers of the young Ptolemy XIII (Pothinus and Achillas), he was stabbed to death directly in his boat, in front of his wife. The arriving Caesar, according to tradition, turned away and wept upon receiving his rival's head — and turned his wrath upon Ptolemy.
level.pompey_death.goal: Ptolemy's court murders Pompey — and Caesar mourns his fallen rival
level.pompey_death.hint: Do not bring Caesar to the harbor — he will spare his rival. Let Ptolemy's court (the eunuch Pothinus, serving the young king) meet the fugitive on the shore; then bring Caesar to the court — they will present him with the head, but he will not reward the killers.
level.pompey_death.intro: Defeated at Pharsalus, Pompey flees to Egypt for refuge. Caesar is ready to forgive his rival — but Ptolemy's court has its own plans.
level.pompey_death.title: The Death of Pompey
level.porphyry.fact: On January 16, 1547, Grand Prince Ivan IV was crowned Tsar in the Dormition Cathedral of the Kremlin, the first to assume the title 'Tsar of All Rus'. Thus, the Russian Tsardom was born.
level.porphyry.goal: The Sovereign of All Rus receives the royal crown
level.porphyry.hint: First, crown Justinian himself — and only then will the reigning emperor elevate Theodora to co-empress. Germanus is not worthy of the crown.
level.porphyry.intro: 527 AD. The heir Justinian ascends the throne. He desires the unprecedented — to crown his wife as full co-empress.
level.porphyry.source: The Rite of Ivan IV's Coronation, 1547
level.porphyry.title: Coronation as Tsar
level.potemkin.fact: Grigory Potemkin, a favorite and, according to rumors, the secret husband of Catherine II, oversaw the annexation of Crimea (1783) and the development of Novorossiya. The annexation of Crimea is a fact; the 'secret marriage' is a rumor; and 'Potemkin villages' are a legend about ostentatious display.
level.potemkin.goal: The all-powerful favorite brings Crimea to the empire.
level.potemkin.hint: Let Catherine first elevate Potemkin to the foremost dignitaries — and only vested with trust will he annex Crimea. The former favorite Orlov will not expand the realm.
level.potemkin.intro: Catherine had many favorites — but only one became a statesman. Grigory Orlov is already in the past.
level.potemkin.title: Potemkin and Crimea
level.prince.fact: Renouncing his cardinalate, Cesare Borgia conquered Romagna with fire and sword, forging his own principality. Niccolò Machiavelli presented his ruthlessness and perfidy as the model of an ideal ruler in his treatise 'The Prince'.
level.prince.goal: Cesare carves out a state for himself in Romagna
level.prince.hint: Let the Pope first equip his son with an army from the Church treasury — and only the equipped Cesare will conquer Romagna. The Pope himself does not take lands.
level.prince.intro: Cesare dreams of carving out a state for himself in Romagna. But without an army, the dream is empty — and the treasury is with his father, the Pope.
level.prince.title: The Prince
level.pugachev.fact: In 1773–1775, the Cossack Yemelyan Pugachev, posing as the 'miraculously saved' Peter III, led the largest rebellion in Russian history. Alexander Suvorov was called upon to suppress it.
level.pugachev.goal: Suvorov captures the impostor, who called himself Peter III.
level.pugachev.hint: Let the impostor first raise a rebellion, calling himself tsar — and only the one who has rebelled will Suvorov capture and condemn. Until he rebels, there is no one to catch.
level.pugachev.intro: Don Cossack Pugachev declared himself the miraculously saved Peter III and raised half of Russia. Suvorov has been sent against him.
level.pugachev.title: Pugachev's Rebellion
level.reconquest.fact: With a small army, Belisarius crushed the Vandal kingdom in Africa (533–534) and reconquered Italy, including Rome, from the Ostrogoths. Justinian's dream of restoring the Roman Empire was almost realized.
level.reconquest.hint: Let Belisarius first crush the Vandals and take Carthage — and only then will the conqueror of Africa reclaim Italy. The glory must be his, not Mundus's.
level.reconquest.intro: Justinian dreams of restoring the West to Rome. Belisarius is ready — but other generals also yearn for glory.
level.reconquest.title: Reconquest of the West
level.reform.fact: Catherine II corresponded with Voltaire and Diderot, convened the Legislative Commission (1767), and wrote the 'Instruction.' Her reign is known as 'enlightened absolutism,' though serfdom only intensified.
level.reform.goal: The Empress gives the empire new laws.
level.reform.hint: Let the empress first be imbued with ideas through correspondence with Diderot — and only then will she issue the enlightened Nakaz. Dignitary Potemkin will not replace the philosopher.
level.reform.intro: Catherine corresponds with Enlightenment philosophers and fancies herself their pupil on the throne.
level.reform.title: The Enlightened Sovereign
level.rivals.fact: The love triangle of Caesar — Cleopatra — Antony was invented by playwrights: Antony became Cleopatra's lover only in 41 BC, three years after Caesar's death. During the dictator's lifetime, he was his loyal general and co-ruler in the consulship.
level.rivals.goal: Caesar and Antony — rivals for the queen's heart
level.rivals.title: Rivals
level.rubicon.fact: On the night of January 10, 49 BC, Caesar, with the XIII Legion, crossed the border river Rubicon, thereby violating the law and initiating civil war against the Senate and Pompey. According to Suetonius, he uttered 'Alea iacta est' — 'The die is cast'.
level.rubicon.goal: Caesar crosses the Rubicon — and Pompey flees Rome
level.rubicon.hint: In the forum, secure a loyal ally. Then meet your rival at the Rubicon — crossing the river sweeps aside whoever stands in the way.
level.rubicon.title: The Die Is Cast
level.sacre.fact: On December 2, 1804, in Notre-Dame Cathedral, Napoleon crowned himself Emperor of the French. In the presence of Pope Pius VII, he placed the crown on his own head — a sign that he owed his power only to himself.
level.sacre.goal: Napoleon crowns himself with the imperial crown
level.sacre.hint: Follow the path: glory → power → crown in Notre-Dame.
level.sacre.title: Coronation of the Emperor
level.streltsy.fact: After suppressing the Streltsy Uprising of 1698, Peter I executed over a thousand Streltsy and disbanded their corps. This reprisal freed his hands for reforms and the creation of a regular army.
level.streltsy.goal: The young Tsar brutally suppresses the Streltsy rebellion.
level.streltsy.hint: Let Sophia's rebellion enrage Peter — and only the furious tsar will become an autocrat with an iron hand. Sophia will not take the throne.
level.streltsy.intro: While Peter strives for Europe, his sister Sophia raises the streltsy behind his back. The rebellion must be drowned in blood.
level.streltsy.title: The Streltsy Uprising
level.tarsus.fact: In 41 BC, Antony summoned Cleopatra to Tarsus for an explanation. She arrived on a gilded barge with purple sails, dressed as Aphrodite — and captivated him with a feast. This marked the beginning of their affair; Antony grew ever more attached to Egypt, drifting away from Rome.
level.tarsus.goal: Cleopatra dazzles Antony — and sways him to the East
level.tarsus.hint: Let the queen appear before the general in dazzling splendor, then captivate him at the feast. Octavian has no place beside Antony — Rome pulls him back.
level.tarsus.intro: Antony summoned Cleopatra to Tarsus to answer for herself — and keeps her at a distance.
level.tarsus.title: The Queen and the General
level.theodora_death.fact: Theodora died in 548 AD, likely from cancer. Justinian, who outlived her by 17 years, never recovered from the loss of his co-ruler and main support. With her death, the 'golden age' of his reign began to wane.
level.theodora_death.goal: The Empress Fades — and the Court's Light Dims
level.theodora_death.hint: Let the emperor be at the bedside of the dying empress — and only after being widowed will he plunge into unending grief. Antonina cannot replace either her or him here.
level.theodora_death.intro: 548 AD. Theodora wastes away from illness. Justinian is at her bedside — and seventeen years of widowhood lie ahead.
level.theodora_death.title: The Death of Theodora
level.thermidor.fact: On July 27, 1794 (9 Thermidor), the Convention rebelled against Robespierre; the next day, he and his associates, including Saint-Just, were guillotined without trial. Thus ended the Terror.
level.thermidor.goal: The Convention deposes the tyrant Robespierre and executes him
level.thermidor.hint: The tyrant is vulnerable: a deputy accuses him in the Convention, then — the guillotine.
level.thermidor.intro: Robespierre — the all-powerful leader of the Terror; the Convention prepares a coup.
level.thermidor.title: Thermidor
level.toulon.fact: In December 1793, 24-year-old artillery captain Napoleon Bonaparte planned the capture of Toulon, occupied by the British. The success earned him the rank of brigadier general and his first widespread fame.
level.toulon.goal: Young Bonaparte gains glory at Toulon
level.toulon.hint: Let Bonaparte first propose a daring artillery plan at the council — and only by his plan shall he take the fort and become a hero. Carteaux sees no key to the city.
level.toulon.intro: 1793. Toulon has surrendered to the English. Incompetent General Carteaux dithers outside the city, while unknown Captain Bonaparte sees a weak point.
level.toulon.title: Siege of Toulon
level.triumvirate.fact: In November 43 BC, Antony, Octavian, and Lepidus formed the Second Triumvirate—a legal alliance to wage war against Caesar's assassins. It began with proscriptions: hundreds of enemies, including Cicero, were outlawed and executed.
level.triumvirate.goal: The triumvirs avenge Caesar — and outlaw his killer
level.triumvirate.hint: First a public alliance, then a secret pact. Bound by the plot, they bring the proscription down on Caesar's killer.
level.triumvirate.title: The Second Triumvirate
level.union.fact: In 1486, Henry VII, a Lancastrian, married Elizabeth of York, uniting the Red and White Roses; their son Arthur solidified the dynasty. But Yorkist pretenders — Lambert Simnel and Perkin Warbeck — challenged the throne for years; Warbeck was executed at the Tower in 1499.
level.union.goal: Henry seals the union of roses, provides an heir, and executes the pretender.
level.union.hint: Marry Elizabeth of York and beget an heir, then send the pretender to the Tower.
level.union.intro: Henry VII weds the Lancastrians to the Yorks — but the pretender Warbeck threatens new turmoil.
level.union.title: Union of Two Roses
level.varennes.fact: On the night of June 21, 1791, Louis XVI and his family secretly fled Paris but were recognized and apprehended in Varennes. The flight shattered the image of the patriot-king and hastened the fall of the monarchy.
level.varennes.goal: The King flees Paris — and is declared a traitor
level.varennes.hint: Let the King first flee disguised — and only then shall a patriot identify and arrest the fugitive in Varennes. The royalist Fersen will not betray the King.
level.varennes.intro: Night of 1791. Louis XVI secretly flees Paris, hoping to reach loyal troops. Loyal Count Fersen drives the carriage.
level.varennes.source: J. Michelet, 'History of the French Revolution'
level.varennes.title: Flight to Varennes
level.waterloo.fact: On June 18, 1815, at Waterloo, Napoleon's army was defeated by the forces of the Duke of Wellington and Prussian Field Marshal Blücher. The Emperor abdicated a second time and was exiled to the island of Saint Helena, where he died in 1821.
level.waterloo.goal: The Coalition deposes the Emperor — and he is sent into exile
level.waterloo.hint: Let the coalition first break the emperor on the field of Waterloo — and only then shall the broken one be exiled to Saint Helena. The undefeated cannot be sent overseas.
level.waterloo.intro: June 1815. Napoleon, returned from Elba, stakes everything on a single battle at Waterloo against Wellington.
level.waterloo.title: Waterloo
level.wrath.fact: In November 1581, Ivan the Terrible, in a fit of rage, fatally wounded his eldest son and heir, Tsarevich Ivan, with his staff. Ilya Repin immortalized the scene. The heir's death doomed the dynasty to extinction.
level.wrath.goal: The Tsar, in a fit of fury, kills his own son.
level.wrath.hint: First the Oprichnina with Malyuta; the heir is then ruined by the Tsar himself in his chambers.
level.wrath.source: I. Repin, 'Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan'
level.wrath.title: The Wrath of the Terrible

Assemble the story from panels —
and discover what truly happened.
ui.onb.1.body: Each level is a real episode. Arrange characters in scenes – if it all fits, the story happens!
ui.onb.1.title: Assemble the Story
ui.onb.2.body: Read left to right: first cause, then effect. Panel order often decides everything!
ui.onb.2.title: Panels: Comic Frames
ui.onb.3.body: Unsure of the order? Drag scenes between panels right on the board!
ui.onb.3.title: Move Scenes
ui.onb.4.body: Extra characters are a decoy! Sometimes, the right move is to leave someone out.
ui.onb.4.title: Not Every Character Is Needed
ui.onb.5.body: Yellow frame: right characters, wrong order. Red: completely off!
ui.onb.5.title: Read the Highlight
ui.onb.6.body: Solve the level to uncover the true story, complete with historical sources!
ui.onb.6.title: Reward: The Truth

ui.tip.1: Drag scenes between panels — order is everything!
ui.tip.2: Extra characters are decoys. Not everyone needs a place.
ui.tip.3: Panel order is cause and effect: friendship, then the dagger!
ui.tip.4: The same character does different things in different scenes.
ui.tip.5: Yellow highlight: right characters, wrong order!
ui.tip.6: Each level is a real historical episode. Solve it to learn what truly happened!
ui.tip.7: One detail changes everything: a feast turns fatal with a dash of poison.
ui.tip.8: Ask yourself: what are three ways to mess this up?
ui.unlock_body: First chapter is free. A one-time purchase unlocks all chapters, including future ones.
ui.wrong_inert: Completely wrong — neither place nor characters
